backlog.spec: In _solve_once, stop a cap stage early when the sum of radii improved by less than 1e-5 relative to the previous stage, and skip straight to cap=1.0. Set the per-stage maxiter to 120 for the early stages and 300 for the last. This saves CPU for more restarts. Keep other code unchanged.
backlog.title: Adaptive per-restart iteration budget

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the cap list with one that is dense only where caps are active and drops the inactive upper part: caps = list(np.arange(0.06, 0.14 + 1e-9, 0.01)) + [1.0] (9 capped stages plus the free stage). Caps above about 0.15 bind almost no circle in a 26-circle packing, so the stages from 0.15 to 0.39 are wasted solves. Keep MAX_ITER, the objective, the constraints and the repair unchanged. Store the list in a module-level constant CAPS.
backlog.title: Truncated dense cap schedule in the active radius range

backlog.spec: In cons, replace the sqrt pair constraint with the smooth form d2 - (r_i+r_j)^2 where d2 is the squared centre distance, clipping r sums at nonnegative values via the existing r>=0 constraints. This removes the non-smooth sqrt at zero distance. Keep the cap continuation and everything else the same.
backlog.title: Squared-distance pair constraints

backlog.spec: Pass ftol to SLSQP that depends on the stage: 1e-4 for the caps below 0.2, 1e-6 for the middle caps, and 1e-10 for the final uncapped stage. Keep the iteration cap as it is. Early stages only need to place the circles roughly, and the tight final stage fixes the sum. Each restart should finish sooner, so more restarts fit in the 80 percent budget.
backlog.title: Loose tolerance early, tight tolerance late

backlog.spec: Change the cap schedule in _solve_once from np.arange(0.05, 0.4+1e-9, 0.02) to a finer grid np.arange(0.06, 0.30+1e-9, 0.03) followed by a few steps 0.35, 0.45 and then 1.0, and cut MAX_ITER per stage to 100. The goal is more restarts at the same quality. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Finer cap continuation schedule

backlog.spec: At the end of each cap stage, find circles whose radius equals the current cap within 1e-6. Remove their radii from the optimisation variables and hold them at that radius for the next stage. Only free circles keep their pair constraints against each other. This reduces the dimension of each SLSQP call as the continuation proceeds. Unfreeze everything for the final uncapped stage so the optimum is still found over all circles.
backlog.title: Freeze circles that hit the cap

backlog.spec: For the first 4 cap stages, replace the pair constraints with the soft version d_ij - r_i - r_j >= -0.01 so early stages allow slight overlap; the later stages use the exact constraints. This smooths early continuation. Implement by adding a margin parameter to cons that is 0.01 for the early stages and 0 for the rest.
backlog.title: Log-sum-exp soft pair constraints early

backlog.spec: Add a second restart type that reuses the continuation as the perturbation. After the first restart, on every other loop iteration take the best packing's centres, add Gaussian jitter of sd 0.01 (clip to [0.02, 0.98]), set all radii to min(r_best, MELT_CAP) with MELT_CAP drawn uniformly from [0.07, 0.11] with the seeded rng, and run the cap continuation only from MELT_CAP upward (caps in the existing list that are >= MELT_CAP, then 1.0). To support this, give _solve_once optional arguments x0 and cap_min. Because the big circles are deflated and regrown while the small ones stay, the packing can rearrange locally without losing its global structure. Keep the result if its repaired sum of radii beats the best. The other half of the iterations remain plain random restarts.
backlog.title: Melt and regrow the incumbent through the cap continuation

backlog.spec: After the restart loop ends, take the best packing (before repair) and run one more SLSQP from it with cap=1.0, maxiter=500 and ftol=1e-12, using the same constraints. Reserve about 1.5 s of CPU for it by lowering the loop's time check accordingly (for example stop restarts at 0.75*time_limit). Accept the polished result only if it is better after _repair. Keep the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Final tight-tolerance SLSQP polish of best

backlog.spec: Give each cap stage its own maxiter instead of MAX_ITER=200 everywhere. Use a small budget (about 60) for the caps 0.05 to 0.2, where the packing is still moving a lot and a rough answer is enough, and a larger budget (about 400) for the caps 0.3, 0.36, 0.4 and the uncapped final stage. Keep the same cap list. The aim is to spend the restart's CPU time where the final sum is decided, which gives more restarts per call.
backlog.title: Per-stage SLSQP iteration budget

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, drop the box constraints c-r, 1-c-r? No: keep the four centre-minus-radius wall constraints, but remove the r >= 0 and cap - r entries from cons. Instead pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0, 1] and radii in [0, cap] for each stage (bounds=[(0,1)]*2n + [(0,cap)]*n). SLSQP handles bounds natively and more cheaply than general inequalities. This removes 2n constraint rows per stage and makes each iteration faster, with the same feasible set.
backlog.title: Move box, cap and nonnegativity constraints into SLSQP bounds

backlog.spec: Combine the two best near-incumbent changes (slots 28 and 16). In _solve_once, on a random half of the restarts (rng.random() < 0.5), place the centres as in slot 28. That means about 4*sqrt(n) circles on a ring near the border (jittered positions at distance about 0.1 from the edges, evenly spaced along the perimeter), with the rest uniform in [0.25, 0.75]^2. On all restarts, set the initial radii to a shuffled power-law profile: r_k proportional to k^-0.5 for k=1..n, scaled so the mean is INIT_RADIUS, then randomly permuted with rng. Keep the cap continuation unchanged. Use rng for all randomness.
backlog.title: Stack perimeter-ring start with power-law radius start

backlog.spec: Remove the last two blocks (r and cap - r) from the constraint vector in cons, so it returns only the pair distances and the four wall blocks. Pass the radius limits natively through the bounds argument of minimize: bounds = [(0, 1)] * (2 * n) + [(0, cap)] * n for each stage (for the final stage use cap = 1.0, i.e. effectively free). Before each stage clip the warm-start radii into [0, cap] so the start respects the bounds. This removes 52 nonlinear-treated constraints from each SLSQP QP subproblem and keeps the centres inside the square exactly, making every restart cheaper and the cap handling exact. Keep the cap list and the repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius limits as SLSQP bounds instead of constraints

backlog.spec: Change the continuation so it starts nearly feasible and grows the cap by a constant ratio. Set INIT_RADIUS = 0.02 and replace the cap list with a geometric sequence: cap_0 = 0.03, cap_{k+1} = 1.18 * cap_k while cap <= 0.16 (about 11 stages), followed by the free stage cap = 1.0. With small initial radii the random start has few overlaps, so the first SLSQP stages are cheap and the circles settle into a spread-out arrangement before they compete; the geometric spacing puts more stages at small caps where the topology is decided and fewer at large caps. Keep MAX_ITER, the constraints and the repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Geometric cap schedule from a feasible small start

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, let the pair constraints in capped stages be d - r_i - r_j + eps >= 0, where eps starts at 0.01 at the first cap and decreases linearly to 0 at the last capped stage (cap 0.4). The final cap=1.0 stage uses eps = 0, so the constraints are exact, and the repair step is unchanged. Allowing a slight overlap early lets circles slide past each other while the structure forms, which avoids early jamming. Only the pair constraints get eps; the wall constraints stay exact.
backlog.title: Annealed overlap allowance during the cap continuation

backlog.spec: For the best packing at the end, alternate up to 5 times: fix the centres and solve the radii exactly with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) maximising sum r subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij and wall constraints; then run a short SLSQP (maxiter 50) over all variables from that point. Keep the result if the repaired sum improves. Use about 1 s of reserved CPU time.
backlog.title: Alternating LP radii and SLSQP centres polish

backlog.spec: Instead of setting every initial radius to INIT_RADIUS=0.05, compute the initial centres first, then set each initial radius to 0.5 times the distance to its nearest other start centre, further capped at the wall distance and at 0.15. Keep the random centres drawn from the same rng. This gives a feasible-looking start with radii matched to local spacing, with no extra random draws.
backlog.title: Nearest-neighbour radius prior at initialisation

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, after each cap stage except the last, add Gaussian noise with sd 0.003 to the centres (clipped to [0.02, 0.98]) and shrink the radii by 3 percent before the next stage. This helps escape jammed states. Seed everything from rng.
backlog.title: Centre jitter between continuation stages

backlog.spec: Move the box and nonnegativity limits out of the constraint vector and into the bounds argument of minimize. Centre coordinates get bounds (0, 1) and radii get bounds (0, cap) for each stage. Keep only the pair-distance constraints in the constraint list, and keep the cap as a bound rather than a constraint row. This shrinks the number of constraint rows from about 6n + n(n-1)/2 to n(n-1)/2, which speeds each SLSQP iteration. The optimum is unchanged.
backlog.title: Native SLSQP bounds for the box and radius limits

backlog.spec: After drawing the random start, reorder the circles so that the largest initial radii come first, and then run the whole continuation in that order. Sorting is done only once per restart and changes no constraint. Because SLSQP's pivoting depends on variable order, this gives a different path through the same problem and is cheap to try. Apply the inverse permutation to the returned centres and radii so the harness sees the original order.
backlog.title: Sort circles by initial radius before SLSQP

memo:
All 40 slots (0-39) are used. Incumbent is still slot 8, the radius-cap SLSQP continuation: -2.6343, one run, never replicated (noise sd 0.0023). It is the only clear win (delta -0.0063). It improved per-restart SLSQP convergence.

Slots 39 (-2.6354), 28 (-2.6360) and 16 (-2.6354) came out lower than the incumbent. Their deltas are -0.0012, -0.0017 and -0.0012, which is within noise. Slots 10, 9 and 15 were neutral. Slots 13, 23, 31, 32 and 36 matched -2.6343 or came within 0.0003 of it.

Hurt: extra stages, other solvers (slots 24, 25), pair pruning (slot 18), start-shape tweaks (19, 20, 29, 30, 34, 35, 37), penalties (26, 27) and schedule priors (38).

Next: replicate slot 8, then replicate slots 28, 16 and 39 and stack the ones that hold. Tune the cap schedule. Avoid new penalties, solvers and start-shape changes.
